title: Embedded with Burnham: The special relationship shrinks
gist: A satirical sketch by Henry Morris imagines new UK prime minister Andy Burnham's first meeting with Donald Trump at the UN General Assembly, mocking a transactional, dominance-obsessed Trump and a shrinking 'special relationship'. Implied serious points: UK priorities on Nato, Patriot missiles for Ukraine, Israeli settlements and the Strait of Hormuz carry little weight against Trump's deal-making style.

insights.claim: In Morris's satirical account, Burnham's agenda for meeting Trump is framed as Nato and Patriot missiles to Ukraine as positives and illegal Israeli settlements and Middle East war as negatives, with the advice to always let Trump think he's winning.
insights.speaker: Henry Morris
insights.so_what: Satire reflects a perceived UK strategy of flattery-based management of Trump to protect Ukraine support.
insights.quote: Always let him think he’s winning.
insights.locator: The tone is set when Andy Burnham

insights.claim: The sketch portrays Trump as dismissing multilateral frameworks in favour of 'strong deals', claiming Putin respects him, saying he told Zelensky 'no more blank cheques' and calling Nato 'total freeloaders'.
insights.speaker: Henry Morris
insights.so_what: Captures the perceived transactional US stance toward Ukraine aid and alliance burden-sharing that underpins European defence spending pressure.

insights.claim: The satire references UK concerns over the Strait of Hormuz and Trump's criticism of the UK 'giving away' islands — a jab at the Chagos Islands deal.
insights.speaker: Henry Morris
insights.so_what: Hormuz disruption and Chagos sovereignty are live UK-US friction points in the satirist's framing.

insights.claim: Morris implies the 'special relationship' is shrinking, with the UK reduced to transactional concessions — satirised as a Trump Arch in Westminster doubling as a military storage complex — in exchange for vapourware promises.
insights.speaker: Henry Morris
insights.so_what: Signals UK elite scepticism about US reliability as an ally under Trump.
